Commentary.Commentary: 211 to win then. Yesterday, Paul Stirling said that 220-230 would have been chaseable. Can he convert that statement into execution? Stay tuned for the run chase...

A better outing for the Irish bowlers but only George Dockrell made a case for himself, with 1/26 in 4 overs. Rankin took 3 wickets but was mighty expensive. The last 5 overs went for 67 but in reality, almost every over looked like a death over. Crucially, only 24 came in the last 3. Will that hurt the Afghans?

Nabi showed how valuable spending time in the middle is, as he took some time to get his eye in and then simply exploded. 81 from just 36 balls is more than an eye candy as Afghanistan were struggling at one stage. The other batsmen just played around Nabi, after the openers could not quite repeat their heroics from Saturday.

Not as high a carnage as last night but still, a 200-plus score for Afghanistan, which should be a good one on this deck. Tonight it was more of a hit-every-ball-out-of-the-park mode and Mohammad Nabi played one of the best T20I innings of all time.

An LBW appeal to end the innings. Not out. Probably pitched outside leg, with Rashid missing his flick and getting hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards mid-wicket and the batsmen take a single. No signal from the umpire, so must have been an inside edge. AFGHANISTAN FINISH ON 210/7!
Full and around leg, swung towards deep mid-wicket for just one.
Full and wide outside off, RK throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge. It does not carry to short third man. A single taken.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Outside off, Khan gets across to swing but earns a top edge. The ball lands in no man's land between mid off and long off and the batsmen take a single.
A yorker outside off, Rashid looks to drive but misses.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Chips this straight back for a single.
Full and wide outside off, a swing and a miss.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Sharafuddin Ashraf walks in next.

OUT! It is not a no ball and Shafiqullah is gone. A length ball outside off, Shafaq looks to go downtown but again, gets more height than distance as on the previous one. Only this time, the ball is well inside the ropes and long off takes it comfortably, with Stuart Thompson being the catcher. They check for the no ball but the replays deem it fine.
Shafiqullah has been caught! But it is a no ball?

SIX! Terrific effort in the end though. A length ball on middle, Shafiqullah looks to clear the leg side but gets more height than required. Simi Singh is ready at the wide long on fence but realizes that the ball is going to go beyond. He leaps and tries to parry it to the fielder running across from mid-wicket but sadly for him and his team, the ball just lobs back beyond the boundary!
ANOTHER WIDE. This is even further than the previous one.
WIDE. Full and well outside off, left alone.
Boyd Rankin is back on. 3-0-42-2 so far.
Tucks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. They pick up a single. The umpire signals a leg bye.
Outside off, a swing and a miss.
Rashid Khan walks in at number 7, replacing Nabi.

OUT! High, high, high, into the atmosphere, ionosphere and stratosphere... travelling towards Delhi... but hang on... it is in Dehradun and magnificently taken! Andy Balbirnie, take a bow. That is a superb catch under pressure. A length ball, around middle, Nabi swings this miles in the air and for a second it seems like the ball has travelled the distance. But then, we realize that he has got more height than distance and when the parabolic curve is completed, Balbirnie is seen waiting for it, with his foot very close to the mid-wicket ropes. He takes it as cool as a cucumber and barely reacts! Nabi waits for a while, asks the umpire, gets confirmation from the fielder but it is referred upstairs. Replays show that the catch is fine and Nabi's maiden T20I century will have to wait. Still, 81 from 36 is not bad at all, is it?
FOUR! WALLOP! Full and around middle, Nabi hits this gun-barrel straight, right over the bowler, for a boundary!
Full and outside off, hit out towards long off for a single.
Peter Chase returns. 2-0-26-0 so far.

FOUR! 25 from the over, 75 from the last 4! This is not getting from bad to worse - albeit from worse to worst for Ireland. A length ball, outside off, Nabi just pulls it with disdain through mid-wicket. There is a man stationed in the deep but he cannot get there!
SIX! High and handsome! Full and outside off, right in the slot. Dispatched over long off!
FOUR! Off the inside edge. A fine yorker, outside off, Nabi gets across to flick but the ball takes the inner half of the bat and goes past short fine leg!
SIX! VIOLENCE! Real violence. A length ball, around middle, Nabi backs away and swings it over long on!
Outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
FOUR! That is some shot to be played on your very first ball. Full and outside off, Shafiqullah gets down and across and scoops it over the keeper to the fine leg fence!
Joshua Little is back on. 2-0-20-0 so far.
A short ball outside off, Mohammad sways away and then looks at the umpire, expecting a wide, but it ain't coming. 18 from the over, 50 from the last 3!
SIX! Now, what to talk about this? It is full and it is outside off. Right in the slot for Nabi who is in murderous mood. Backs away, gets right under the ball and dispatches it over cover.
SIX! TONK! A short ball this time, Nabi clears his front leg and swings this right over the sightscreen!
FOUR! Super shot. A length ball outside off, Nabi backs away to the leg side and hits this inside out over cover for a boundary!
A length ball, Nabi goes back and looks to pull but gets a top edge. Luckily for him, it does not carry to deep square leg. A couple taken.
Shafiqullah Shafaq walks in at number 7, replacing Najibullah.

OUT! DIRECT HIT, BULL'S EYE! We need not have a second look, it looked so out. Wonder why it was referred upstairs. A short ball, Najibullah pulled it straight to George Dockrell at short mid-wicket and took off for the single. George fielded, picked it up, took aim and then released a powerful throw - direct at the base of the stumps at the bowler's end. Zadran started to walk immediately as he knew he was gone. But the umpire wanted to be sure.
Direct hit! Is Zadran gone? Referred upstairs... but Najibullah is walking...
Boyd Rankin is back on. 2-0-24-2 so far.
FOUR! A high full toss, around middle, Nabi whips it over short fine leg and gets a boundary! 19 from the over - after going for 2 in his first.

Oops... A wide yorker outside off, Mohammad looks to dig it out but gets a bottom edge. The ball rolls back towards the stumps but the batsman is more interested in the single. He is then asked by his partner to stop the ball first which he does.

SIX! THWACK! Probably the biggest of the night. Slower ball, fuller in length outside off, Nabi picks it, waits for it and then swings it into oblivion over mid-wicket! 35 from just 23 balls now. The stand meanwhile, has moved to 32 from 15 deliveries.
Outside off, pushed towards cover-point for a run.
A high full toss, around middle, Mohammad misses his heave and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. A single taken.
SIX! Outstanding shot. Full and outside off, Nabi reaches out and just carves it over cover! Tell you, it is definitely not an easy shot to play. Superb batting.
WIDE. Full and miles outside off, Nabi reaches out to drive but misses.
Around off, worked through mid-wicket for one. 13 from the over, yet, Dockrell finishes with figures of 4-0-26-1. Superb spell.
Full and outside off, pushed past the bowler towards long off for a run.
SIX! THUNDEROUS! Zadran is slowly coming to the party now. Full and around off, Najibullah gets down and plays the slog sweep miles over mid-wicket!
FOUR! Nice shot! Full and around middle and leg, Zadran gets his bat down and reverse sweeps it precisely between short third man and backward point. Superb picking of the gap.
Around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

This is slightly around leg, NZ misses his flick and is hit on the pads. A mild LBW appeal ensues and the batsmen are distracted, with Zadran halfway down the track for the single and Nabi looking at the bowler. In the end, a mishap is averted.
Full and around off, pushed through mid off for a run.
Another leg bye as Najibullah misses a tuck again. The ball was pitched outside leg.
Full and wide outside off, steered down to third man for a single.
Down the leg side, Zadran misses his flick and is hit on the pads. A leg bye taken towards square leg.
Najibullah Zadran walks in at number 6, replacing his skipper.

OUT! Getkate strikes first ball! Full and outside off, Afghan gets under it and looks to hit it over long off but the lack of pace defeats him. Hence he mistimes his shot and finds Stuart Thompson at long off. The budding 40-run stand is broken at the right time.
Shane Getkate into the attack now. 7th bowler for the evening.
Full and around off, watchfully defended. 10 from the over, 23 from the last 2.
Outside off, punched towards long on again for another single.
Outside off, punched down to long on for one.
SIX! THUMP! Downtown goes Nabi. Flighted on middle, Mohammad comes down the track and sends it sailing over long on! 103 metres on the radar.
Comes down the track and hoicks it over square leg for a run.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover who misfields and concedes a single.
Full and around middle, nicely controlled flick towards backward square leg for a run. 13 from the over. Chase's figures read 2-0-26-0 so far.
ANOTHER WIDE. 5th of the night already. Down the leg side, Nabi misses his flick.
A full toss outside off, Afghan is surprised by that as he just pushes it back to the bowler. Chase fumbles and lets it through. A single taken.
WIDE. This one definitely is wided. Full and miles outside off, left alone.
A slower ball bouncer, outside off, Asghar lets it go, thinking it will be wided but it isn't.
FOUR! THRASH! Banged in short, Afghan goes back and swats it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Dropped short now, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Welcome into the attack, my friend! Full and wide outside off, a gentle loosener, Nabi reaches out and lofts it casually over cover!
Peter Chase into the attack now.
Fired in on leg stump, Mohammad misses his tuck and is hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards square leg and a leg bye is taken. 84/3 at the halfway stage.
A touch quicker, short and around middle, helped through square leg for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

Around off, skids through, Nabi pushes this uppishly again and once more it falls short of the bowler. However, Dockrell misfields while going to his right and the ball goes to long on. A single taken.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and around off, pushed back a tad uppishly back to the bowler. Does not carry.
SIX! Ho ho ho! Even better! A long hop again, around middle, Asghar swivels and pulls it over mid-wicket. This time clearing the ropes! The last 2 balls just spoil the over...
FOUR! THRASH! Short and outside off, Afghan pulls it over mid-wicket and gets his first boundary.
Full and wide outside off, squeezed behind point for a single.
Short and outside off, Mohammad cuts it behind point. Peter puts in a good chase to his right from third man, slides and stops the ball. Two runs taken.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
WIDE. Well outside off, Nabi flashes hard but misses.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Another watchful defense means that Dockrell has gone for just 2 runs in his opening over, taking a wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Mohammad Nabi walks in at number 5, replacing Tarakai.

OUT! Taken at long on and the hard-hitting Tarakai departs too! Intelligent bowling but not-so intelligent batting. Full and around off, Najeeb gets down and looks to play the slog sweep. Is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and only skies it high in the air. Andy Balbirnie comes running in from long on and takes a decent catch. Three big hitters depart, in the span of 22 balls.
Quicker and flatter outside off, solidly defended.
On a slightly shorter length outside off, pushed towards the off side for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Proper spin time. George Dockrell called upon to bowl.
Finally gets off the mark on the 7th ball. Pushes this through the covers and gets across.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Now a wild swing, outside off, missed again.
Outside off, Afghan throws his bat at that with his feet stuck in mud. Misses.
On middle and leg, helped through mid-wicket for a single.
Stuart Thompson comes in to bowl now.
Full and around off, driven down the ground towards long on for a run. 64/2 in the Powerplay.
Outside off, Najeeb looks to punch it through the off side but is beaten as the ball nips back in.
Outside off, punched straight to point.
FOUR! Great shot. A length ball outside off, Tarakai reaches out and drives it through cover-point for a boundary!
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. One run added to the total. The umpire signals a leg bye.
A length ball outside off, Afghan swings wildly but misses.
WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
In comes the skipper, Asghar Afghan at number 4, replacing Zazai.

OUT! That is a 'sterling' catch and the Irish are pumped up! Not much of Zazai's fireworks tonight. A length ball, outside off, Hazratullah swings hard but is way too early into the shot. Gets a big leading edge which goes a long way up in the air. Now, this is a tricky catch. Paul Stirling is at mid off and has to run backwards to go for the catch. He puts in the hard yards, keeps his eyes on the ball and dives at the last moment to take a two-handed stunner! The entire camp in Green is hugging its skipper. Now, now, now, do they believe? We almost had everything in that over - A four, a six, a dropped catch and 2 wickets. Wow.

DROPPED! That would have been a great catch, had it been taken. A length ball, on middle, Tarakai looks to help it over the man at short fine leg but cannot quite get the elevation. The ball travels thick and fast to the right of Peter Chase who throws himself to his right but cannot hang on. A single taken.
SIX! THRASH! Full and around off, Tarakai swings it over mid-wicket and the ball travels a mile!
FOUR! Swung over mid on! Well, Tarakai has seen just one ball and gone bang on the next. A length ball, around off, Najeeb swings it but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat over mid on!
Around off, tucked straight to short mid-wicket.
Najeeb Tarakai comes in at number 3, replacing Ghani.

OUT! LBW! The tall Rankin has struck! There falls the first wicket. Pace has done it for Ireland. A skiddy ball, pitched on a good length outside off, Ghani stays back in his crease to play that to the on side but misses. The speed does him in, beating his attempt and hitting him on the back pad. It is below the knee roll as well and Rankin appeals long and hard. The umpire thinks for a while and eventually raises his finger! Can Ireland build on this?

Boyd Rankin changes ends. 1-0-13-0 so far. Well, the sightscreen issues crop up again. Meanwhile, some sawdust is being brought on to be put in the bowler's landing area. Just 4 overs bowled in the first 25 minutes...
Another similar delivery, let through once more. 14 from this one, 41 from the last 3!
Full and outside off, almost flirting with the wide guidelines, left alone. The umpire passes that as a legal ball.

FOUR! Oh my my! This is some shot from Hazratullah. The ball is full and wide outside off and Zazai has to reach out for it. He does so, but in the process, loses control. The bottom hand comes off his bat but still, the ball hits the sweet spot of the bat and flies over cover!
WIDE! Oh dear... this is pressure on the bowler. Bowls it outside the pitch, wayyy outside off. Stuart Poynter collects it almost at first slip.
FOUR! TAKE THAT! Nothing streaky about this one. Full and outside off, Zazai swings this right back over the bowler, through mid on and down to the fence. The stand is worth 41 from 21 balls now.

FOUR! Streaky boundary. Full and wide outside off, Zazai throws his bat at it and ends up getting a thick outside edge. Luckily for him, it flies over short third man. In hindsight, that was not a good ball. With third man up, one cannot bowl wide outside off.
Around off, on a length, whipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Joshua Little into the attack now. Stirling will hope that he concedes 'little' runs in this over.
Full and outside off, HZ comes down the track and swings wildly but misses. 13 from that over.

FOUR! Fantastic connection from Zazai. Carnage from both ends now. Short and around middle, Hazratullah swivels and pulls it behind square leg. Fine leg starts to run to his right but the moment the ball makes contact with the turf, it just races away. Third boundary of the over. The stand moves to 32 from 17 balls.
Around off, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! And another! Full and around off, Ghani gets across and flicks it handsomely over backward square leg! One bounce and into the ropes once more. Moves to 11 from 6 balls.
FOUR! SPANKED! The attack has begun. A length ball outside off, Ghani comes down the track and swings it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Around off, tight line to start, solidly defended.
Peter Chase comes on to bowl. The Simi experiment lasted just one over.
SIX! There he goes! First biggie of the night! A length ball, around off, Zazai gets underneath this and swings it mightily over long on! 10 from the last 2, which means 14 have come from the over.
FOUR! First boundary of Sunday. Of how many? Full and around off, Zazai drives this beautifully down the ground and comfortably beats mid off!
Short and outside off, flashed down to third man for one.
This one hurried the batsman, looking to tuck him up, Hazratullah missed his tuck and the ball went off his pads towards long leg. A leg bye taken.
Nice shot. Fractionally short in length outside off, Ghani gets back and across and plays a Nataraja pull shot through square leg for a run.
A short ball, down the leg side, comfortably pulled towards fine leg for a single.
Boyd Rankin to bowl from the other end. A slight delay as there are sightscreen issues. Two lights protrude from behind the black screen and those are causing some disturbance, understandably.
Full and around off, swung towards deep mid-wicket for a run. A watchful start by the hosts.
Landed outside off, punched down to long on for a single.
Flicks this away and gets to the other end.
Goes for another sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and down the leg side, Zazai gets down and paddles it fine for a couple.

We are all ready for the game to begin then. Interesting choice from Stirling. Simi Singh has been given the new ball. The destroyers from last night - Hazratullah Zazai and Usman Ghani will open for Afghanistan. Zazai to face. Here we go...

Afghanistan skipper, Asghar Afghan, opines that he would have liked to bat first as well. On the areas of improvement for this game, Asghar says that bowling under dewy conditions will be challenging. Informs that the side has made 4 changes.

Ireland captain, Paul Stirling, says that the team would want to try and correct the mistakes from last night, hence the decision to field on the same pitch. Admits that the team needs a much improved performance today and be selective in their shot-making.
TOSS TIME. Once again, Asghar flips the coin and this time, finally Stirling calls it correctly. IRELAND OPT TO CHASE.
PITCH REPORT - Niall O'Brien it is again, with the pitch report. For today, he says that it looks like an absolute ROAD. Advises the captain winning the toss to bat first.

Rashid Khan says that he just tries to repeat what he did in previous games, doing the basics right and trying to bowl in the right areas. Stresses that as a professional, one needs to understand that dew will be around and accordingly adjust.
WEATHER - Much better climate than the first 2 games. The sun has already set and twilight scenes are on display. Crucially, no rain clouds around.

Beaten in game 1. Hammered in game 2. What will be the outcome of the third? The series is done and dusted but neither side will take this lightly. Afghanistan will be hungry for their 10th successive T20I win over Ireland, while the visitors will aim to stop that losing rut. Hello and a warm welcome to the third and final T20I between Afghanistan and Ireland in Dehradun.
